sample_measured_here.data_caveat_found_here: price_delta_bps is DEGENERATE in this split: every value lies in [-10000.0, -9999.9]. It differences a Polymarket probability (0..1) against a Binance USD price (~80949), so the field is a unit-mismatch sentinel, not a spread. Do not consume this column.

why_this_matters_to_the_desk.headline: The corpus's realised value here is METHODOLOGICAL, not directional, and it was banked without ingesting the full split.
why_this_matters_to_the_desk.l1_46_corroboration: Every lag_pairs row declares THREE clocks -- binance_source_ts_ms, polymarket_source_ts_ms (venue stamps) and paired_at_ms (collector stamp) -- which is exactly the discipline L1.46 installed here after 82% of desk data was found carrying an undeclared clock. An outside team, independently, treats t_venue and t_recv as separate first-class columns.
why_this_matters_to_the_desk.the_measured_warning: The paper reports a 16ms median lag on venue source clocks, relative clock drift bounded to <=6ms, and a RESIDUAL SINGLE-VANTAGE CONSTANT-OFFSET AMBIGUITY OF ~+/-99ms. Measured here on the sample: median lead_lag +14ms with IQR [-38, +92]ms. THE DECLARED AMBIGUITY IS THE SIZE OF THE ENTIRE INTERQUARTILE RANGE. A single-vantage collector cannot resolve a sub-100ms cross-venue lead-lag, however carefully it stamps -- not a data-quality failing, a structural limit of observing two venues from one point.
why_this_matters_to_the_desk.their_response_to_it: They fall back to a SYNCHRONIZATION-FREE event study measured only on the collector clock, which independently shows Polymarket quotes responding to large Binance moves after a median 347ms. That is the robust estimand: an interval on ONE clock, never a difference between two.
why_this_matters_to_the_desk.measured_here_supporting_that: paired_at_ms - binance_source_ts_ms has median 6213ms (p95 18698ms) in the sample -- the collector clock is seconds away from the venue stamp, so the two bases are not interchangeable even approximately.
why_this_matters_to_the_desk.bears_on: R0117 (cross-venue quote lead-lag at own synchronized L2 timestamps), already flagged in L1.46 as resting on a false premise via sampling-phase aliasing. This is a SECOND, independent reason the same row cannot work as specified: even with perfect sampling phase, a single-vantage constant-offset ambiguity remains. Rowed separately.

reopen_condition_l1_16a: A named orthogonal use that does NOT re-run the graveyarded construction -- e.g. using the corpus as a labelled ground-truth fixture to validate the desk's own cross-venue timing methodology against a corpus whose clock provenance is fully declared. Absent that, the full 727M-row split stays un-ingested.
